info.title: akou
info.description: The akou API over HTTP. Every operation is marked with the modes that serve it (`x-akou-modes`: the desktop app, server mode, or both) and the key it needs (`x-akou-access`). Generated from the route table; do not edit by hand.

get.description: What akou is doing now: the app, the live call if there is one with its state and health, and the last call.
Every setting: its value, the values set in the config file, problems found in the file, and the schema of each key. Secrets are redacted.

patch.description: Change settings: a JSON object of dotted keys to new values, `null` to unset one. Every value is checked against the settings registry; one bad key refuses the whole change.

get.description: The note templates the enhanced notes can use: the shipped ones and the user's own, with the sections of each.
The read-only live links that are on, one per shared call.

post.description: Start a read-only live link to a call (default `live`). `bind` is `tailnet`, `lan` or an IPv4 address; `notes` also shares the notepad; `expires` is a duration such as `2h`.

delete.description: Stop the live link of one call, or every link when no call is named.

post.description: Show the window, on a call if one is named. With no window (headless) the answer is the address of the window in a browser, with a one-time code.
Quit akou cleanly, after the answer is sent. A live call is stopped first.

get.description: The speech models on disk: `missing`, `downloading` with bytes so far, `ready` or `failed`.

post.description: Download every missing model file, each checked against its pinned SHA-256. Answers at once: 202 while the download runs, 200 when the models are already there. Follow it with models.get.

Start recording a call. `workspace` and `title` name it; `template` picks the notes template; `call` and `mic` pick the sources; `vocab` adds words for this call; `withoutModels` records before the speech models are downloaded. One call at a time: a second start answers 409.

get.description: The calls on disk, newest first, by metadata only: id, title, workspace, times and state. Never their content.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many calls.

parameters.name: workspace
parameters.description: Only the calls of this workspace.

parameters.name: failed
parameters.description: List only the calls whose start failed.

get.description: One call: its title, workspace, state, parts, speakers, health, the final pass and the log cursor.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

post.description: Stop recording the live call. The final pass runs after it on its own.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

post.description: Pause the live call: nothing is recorded until resume.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

post.description: Resume a paused call.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

post.description: Mute the microphone channel of the live call; the call channel keeps recording.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

post.description: Unmute the microphone channel.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

post.description: Start a new part of a call: a live call rebuilds its capture, an ended call records a new part into the same folder and log. An ended call whose last audio is over an hour old needs `force`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

get.description: The call's log events after a cursor, oldest first, each exactly once, with the next cursor. With `wait`, holds the request until an event arrives or the wait ends: a long poll.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The log cursor: only events after this `seq`.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Seconds to hold the request while nothing is past the cursor, up to 30.

get.description: The call's log events after a cursor as server-sent events, then every new one as it is written, plus the line being spoken and the levels. A reconnecting client sends `Last-Event-ID` and resumes after it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The log cursor: only events after this `seq`.

get.description: The call's transcript, every line with its local wall-clock time and speaker. `layer` picks the live lines, the final pass, or the best of both; `from`, `to`, `speaker` and `since` narrow it; `limitTokens` keeps the newest lines that fit.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

parameters.name: layer
parameters.description: Which transcript: the final pass for the parts it has finished and the live lines for the rest (`best`), or one of the two.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: JSON lines, Markdown, plain text, or the transcript section of the export.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only lines written or revised after this log position.

parameters.name: limitTokens
parameters.description: Keep the newest lines that fit in this many tokens.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Lines ending at or after this time: epoch ms or ISO 8601.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Lines starting at or before this time: epoch ms or ISO 8601.

parameters.name: speaker
parameters.description: Only this speaker, by id (`c2`) or by name.

post.description: A small, cited context for a question about the call: the lines that answer it, the memo and the call's state, within `budget` tokens. Changes nothing.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

get.description: Search one call's transcript for words, best matches first, each hit with its citation and lines. Never searches across calls.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The words to look for.

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: At most this many hits.

post.description: Ask the configured provider a question about the call and get its cited answer, written to the log as an `answer` event. `stream` sends the answer as server-sent events while it is written.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

post.description: Name a speaker of the call: `spk` is the speaker id (`you`, `c2`), `name` the name to show.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

post.description: Merge speaker `from` into speaker `into`: one person the diarizer split in two.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

post.description: Undo a merge: speaker `spk` is its own speaker again.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

get.description: The call's notepad lines, each with its time and author.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

post.description: Add a line to the call's notepad, marked with its author. `w` is when the line was begun (epoch ms) and `afterSeq` the last transcript position seen then.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

patch.description: Replace the text of one notepad line. The old text stays in the log.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

parameters.name: nid
parameters.description: The note id (`n0012`).

delete.description: Delete one notepad line. The log keeps it, with the delete after it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

parameters.name: nid
parameters.description: The note id (`n0012`).

post.description: Keep a line of agent memory on the call, marked as the agent's.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

delete.description: Forget one line of agent memory. The log keeps it, with the delete after it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

parameters.name: rid
parameters.description: The memory id (`r0012`).

get.description: The call's running memo, the log position it covers, and the current cursor, so a reader can tell whether it is stale.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

put.description: Write the call's running memo, covering the log up to `coversSeq`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

get.description: The vocabulary in force for a call: its own words, the files it used, the pass's proposals, and the words waiting for the user's review.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

post.description: Add a word to this call only: `term` as it should read, `heard` the ways the recognizer wrote it, `segs` the lines it corrects. It applies to reading at once and to decoding from now on; `decode: false` keeps it out of decoding.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

delete.description: Retract a word added to this call. The log keeps it, with the retraction after it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

parameters.name: vid
parameters.description: The entry id (`v0012`).

post.description: Run the vocabulary pass on an ended call: the configured provider corrects known words and proposes new ones. A proposal does nothing until the user approves it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

get.description: The user's vocabulary: the files read and their entries, global and for a workspace.

parameters.name: workspace
parameters.description: The workspace whose file this is; default: the global file.

parameters.name: unconfirmed
parameters.description: Only the entries waiting for the user's yes.

post.description: Add or update a word in the user's vocabulary file. A word the user stated goes in confirmed; send `confirmed: false` for an inferred one, which does nothing until the user approves it.

delete.description: Remove a word from the user's vocabulary file.

parameters.name: term
parameters.description: The word, as written in the file.

parameters.name: workspace
parameters.description: The workspace whose file this is; default: the global file.

post.description: Approve words: unconfirmed entries of the file, or a call's proposals when `call` is named, which are then written into the file, confirmed.
Reject words: unconfirmed entries of the file, or a call's proposals when `call` is named. A rejected word is not proposed again.
Import a word list into the user's vocabulary file, confirmed: one word per line, or the predecessor's `Word <= heard | heard` lines.
Ranked candidate words from a call or from a text, leaving out words already known or rejected. Suggests only; nothing is written.
How the recognizer's tokenizer splits a word. Not built yet: answers 501.

Run the final pass on an ended call, the best transcript akou can make. Answers at once; the pass runs after. It runs by itself after every call, so this is for a pass that failed or for `force` to run it again.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

post.description: Write the call's enhanced notes with the configured provider, from the transcript and the user's notepad, in a template's sections, citing the transcript. With no provider, an agent writes them with enhanced.context and enhanced.put.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

get.description: What an agent needs to write the enhanced notes itself: the instructions, the input built from the transcript and the notepad, and the log position it covers. Send the result with enhanced.put.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

parameters.name: template
parameters.description: The template to use; default: the call's own.

put.description: Store enhanced notes an agent wrote, covering the log up to `coversSeq`. Citations are checked against the transcript and the user's notes are kept.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

get.description: The call's enhanced notes as Markdown, the latest revision or the one `rev` names, with the list of revisions.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

parameters.name: rev
parameters.description: One revision; default: the latest.

get.description: The audio of one part of the call, as Ogg. Honours `Range`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

parameters.name: part
parameters.description: The part number, from 1.

post.description: Export an ended call as Markdown with frontmatter into the export folder, or into the absolute folder `to` names. Answers the file written, and whether it went beside a copy the user edited.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

post.description: Run the call's hand-off hooks again and wait for them: the hooks of `stage` (call.ended, final.done, enhanced), or of every stage the call has reached. The export and the webhook are not re-run.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The call: its id, or `live`. GET routes, the questions and the post-call actions also take `last`.

post.description: Import call folders recorded by the predecessor tool, hark-viewer, as akou calls. `dirs` are absolute folders.

get.description: What this akou is and can do: its version and mode, the presets and whether each is available, the engines, and which capabilities (jobs, events, the OpenAI route) exist. Needs no key.
The calling key: its id, name, scopes and creation time. The app's own token answers as `app` with the `admin` scope. Executor's health check calls it.
This API's OpenAPI 3.1 description, for the running mode. Needs no key. `scope=jobs` lists only the operations a `jobs` key can call, with no compatibility route.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: `jobs`: only what a key with the `jobs` scope can call.

bearerAuth.description: An akou key (`ak_…`) or, on the desktop, the app's token. The key's scope decides which operations it may call.

Error.description: An error, in the one error shape.

message.description: What went wrong, for a person.
